action.rationale: First round with dim=10 and total budget=100 (< 20·dim=200), so run light probes (P1–P3) to learn global structure without burning budget. This will inform whether to go local (lbfgsb/bobyqa) or global (cma_es/turbo) on this cheap, deterministic problem.

Probes indicate global structure (P2 fdc_spearman=0.608) but no clear clustering (top10_spread_vs_uniform=0.987), and with only 88 evaluations left we lack P4/P5 to disambiguate. A short race (18 evals ≈ 20% of total) between cma_es and turbo will hedge and pick the better global method before committing.

CMA-ES won the race decisively (623.8 vs 1637.8) and hasn’t actually run beyond the 9-eval rung yet (sigma=2.87, generation=0, not converged). Probes indicate global structure (P2 fdc=0.61) while top10 spread ~0.99 suggests multiple basins, so a local polish now would be premature. Continuing CMA-ES for a full round should improve or confirm this basin before we consider polishing.

Only 20 evaluations remain (< 1 round), while CMA-ES has stalled for 64 evals with 0 improvement; polishing is the best use of the end budget. BOBYQA needs 2·dim+1 = 21 evaluations to start (dim=10), exceeding the remaining budget. The problem is deterministic and P2 fdc=0.608 suggests usable structure, so LBFGSB from the incumbent is appropriate.
